title: Release Goodness Index & Governance Diary
body:
Overview:
This sheet defines a compact, repeatable "Goodness Index" for releases and a lightweight governance diary for decisions during phased rollouts. Purpose is to give stakeholders a single-number orientation and a reproducible checklist + decision log so go/no-go calls are fast and auditable.

Goodness Index (GI) - design notes:
- A 0-100 index that combines safety, performance, cost, and quality signals.
- Each metric below has a weight, a green/yellow/red threshold, and an owner who is accountable for corrective action.
- GI is recalculated each monitoring window (30m) during canary and hourly once wider.

Metric,Definition,Weight,Owner,Green threshold,Yellow threshold,Red threshold,Current value,Notes
Latency P95,Inference P95 across prod traffic,25%,SRE,<=120ms,121-220ms,>220ms,140ms,slight uptick after traffic shift
Error Rate,5xx + model-timeout per 1k requests,20%,SRE,<=0.5,0.6-1.5,>1.5,0.9,errors concentrated on long sequences
Quality Regression (%fail),Automated eval set delta vs baseline,20%,Applied ML,<=1%,1-3%,>3%,0.8%,within tolerance
Cost per 1k tokens,Estimated $ per 1k served tokens,10%,Finance/Product,<=$0.60,$0.61-$1.00,>$1.00,$0.72,expected with new batching
Cache Hit Rate,Prefix/KV cache effectiveness,10%,Platform,>=70%,50-69%,<50%,65%,tunable TTL
Uptime (api),User-facing availability window,10%,SRE,>=99.95,99.8-99.94,<99.8,99.96%,ok
User-facing latency degradation,User complaints & synthetic user journey P95,5%,Customer Success,<=2% increase,2-5%,>5%,1.2%,no complaints

GI formula: round( Sum_i metric_score_i * weight_i ), metric_score_i in [0..100], derived from thresholds. Example current GI: 84/100.

Release readiness quick digest (one-line): GI 84 — proceed with phase-2 (50% traffic) with watch windows extended to 2h and SRE on immediate pager for first 60 minutes.

Governance diary (live decision log) - canonical format:
Date,Time,Actor,Decision,Rationale,Immediate Actions,Follow-ups,Artifact Links
2024-10-21,09:12,Maya Patel,Canary start @ 10:00,Preflight green,Start canary 5% traffic; schedule 15-min check-ins; notify CS,#REL-1282,https://jira.redwood/browse/REL-1282
2024-10-21,10:35,Liam Chen,Hold increase to 20%,Observed P95 rise to 180ms at 12% traffic,Rollback to 5% for 10m; SRE investigate top n requests,Open SRE ticket,SRE-401
2024-10-21,10:50,Diego Ruiz,Resume to 12%,Mitigation applied (cache TTL tuned),Monitor 30m,Follow-up postmortem,https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/345
2024-11-05,14:20,Maya Patel,Phase-2 start (50%),Quality gating passed and GI=86,Enable feature flags for 50%; enable extended traces for A/B cohort,Schedule QA re-eval in 48h,CONFLUENCE-PHASE2

Preflight checklist (must be green before increasing traffic):
- [ ] Baseline GI computed and shared with stakeholders (link to GI snapshot)
- [ ] Canary harness configured (traffic shard, sampling keys)
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards: latency, errors, model-quality, cache-hit, cost — verified
- [ ] Alerting rules validated for rapid escalation (pager on-call assigned)
- [ ] Rollback plan documented with automated job to cut traffic by 80% within 2 minutes
- [ ] Customer success notified with canned messaging templates
- [ ] Legal/compliance signoff for model or policy changes (when applicable)

Runbook excerpts (short form):
- Rapid rollback: run script infra/traffic_cut --percent 80 --target release-tag; confirm traffic drop via dashboard within 2 minutes.
- If P95 > 220ms or Error Rate > 1.5/1k for >2 consecutive 5m windows: trigger immediate rollback and tag incident SRE-CRIT.
- For quality regressions >3%: pause rollout, revert model (if feature-flagged) or roll to last verified model hash, notify ML leads.

Monitoring queries (examples for dashboards/alerts):
- Influx/PromQL (example): sum(rate(api_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(api_requests_total[5m])) * 1000 AS errors_per_k
- P95 latency (prom): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Cache hit: sum(kv_cache_hits) / (sum(kv_cache_hits) + sum(kv_cache_misses))

Ownership and rotation (first 72h cadence):
- Day 0-1: Product ops lead (Maya) primary, SRE on pager, Platform on standby, ML on-call watches quality signals.
- Day 2-3: Hand off to Ops steward (Liam), daily checkpoint with CS.
- Documentation: every decision must be appended to this diary with artifacts linked.

Contingency action matrix (triage guide):
- Low severity (GI drop 2-6 pts): throttle rollout by 10-20%, increase sampling for traces, tune batching, re-evaluate in 30m.
- Medium (GI drop 7-15 pts OR sustained 2 of 3 metrics yellow): pause rollout, engage platform and ML, run targeted A/B switchback, estimate fix ETA.
- High (>15 pts OR any red in Latency/Error/Quality): immediate rollback to last-green, post-incident review, customer outreach.

Communication templates (short):
- Internal incident stub (Slack #prodops): "[REL-1282] Observed P95 spike at {time}. Taking traffic to 5%. SRE investigating. TL;DR: mitigation -> cache TTL change. Owner: @liam"
- Customer advisory (CS): "We observed increased response latency for a subset of requests and have throttled traffic while we mitigate. No data exposure. ETA for full restore: T+3h."

How to use this sheet daily:
1) Update "Current value" column from monitoring snapshots (automated ETL ideally).
2) Recompute GI; if GI < 75 auto-signal review.
3) Write a short dated diary entry for every manual decision.
4) Attach artifacts (traces, PRs, tickets) to diary entries.

Appendix - quick links and runbooks:
- Canary config doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/pages/CANARY-CONFIG
- Rollback automation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/blob/main/traffic_cut.sh
- Oncall rota: https://docs.redwood/oncall/2024-q4

Notes and open questions (notes-to-self style):
- Explore adding a user-impact weight that pulls from CS tickets rather than synthetic journeys.
- Consider auto-suspension if GI drops >10 within a 15m window (safety circuit).
- Need to coordinate with finance on cost threshold alerts when cost per 1k delta > 25% vs baseline.

End of sheet.
